title: Review Checkpoint Judge
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Evaluation activity in which learners judge, for eight agent steps in an analysis workflow, whether a human review checkpoint is required before the output is used, and select the main reason: Reversibility, Outward effect, Reported result, or No criterion applies. Each committed judgment gets Correct, Right decision, different reason, or Not quite feedback with a one-sentence Why, and each run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and the list of steps judged incorrectly.

educational.topic: Placing human review checkpoints in agent workflows
learningObjectives: Judge, for each of eight agent steps in an analysis workflow, whether a human review checkpoint is required before its output is used, agreeing with the answer key on at least 7 of 8 steps
Justify each judgment by naming the main criterion that applies (reversibility, outward effect, or reported result) or stating that no criterion applies
prerequisites: Output that leaves your control by being sent, published, or used to commit resources
Output that becomes a reported result

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are a native HTML select and native buttons reachable with the Tab key; correct, partly correct, and incorrect feedback uses words and symbols as well as color; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Choose the main reason
controls.purpose: Selects the main reason for the judgment: Reversibility, Outward effect, Reported result, or No criterion applies. Starts on the placeholder for every step; a judgment cannot be committed until a reason is chosen. Disabled after the commit.

controls.label: Review required
controls.purpose: Commits the judgment Review required together with the selected reason for the current step. Disabled after the commit.

controls.label: No review needed
controls.purpose: Commits the judgment No review needed together with the selected reason for the current step. Disabled after the commit.

controls.label: Next Step / See Score / Run Again
controls.purpose: Enabled after a commit. Advances to the next step, shows the score after the eighth step, and on the summary screen starts a new run with the steps reshuffled.

controls.label: More Missed Steps
controls.purpose: Shown only on the summary screen when the list of steps judged incorrectly does not fit on one page; pages through the list.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Criterion-based judgment with a required justification, immediate explanatory feedback, and a reshuffled second run
keyQuestions: Does this output need your review before it is used?
Does the output leave your control by being sent, published, or used to commit resources?
Does the output become a result you will report?
commonMisconceptions: Every agent action needs review, so review is never a choice
A step that looks harmless needs no review even when it is irreversible
A step that only drafts something is safe to send without review
assessmentOpportunities: First-run score of at least 7 of 8 judgments matching the answer key is evidence of mastery
Right decision, different reason results show judgments not yet backed by the correct criterion
Comparison of the first and second run scores shows whether the criteria transferred to a new step order
Learner explains each missed step using the Why sentence and the three criteria
